why: Demanding a script named exactly `typecheck` charged the repository for the VOCABULARY and not for the practice — the same mistake the `tests` rule made with Portuguese file names, in a checker written in Portuguese. Measured: prumo (`"tipos": "tsc -b"`) and ducado (`"tipos"` at the root and `"typecheck"` in three packages) were accused of having no typecheck while both had the script. This variant isolates the NAME branch: the `pass` side has `tipos` and nothing else. The accepted list is still a list of script NAMES, and the `fail` side shows why — it runs `tsc -b` INSIDE `empacotar`, which is exactly the failure the base case describes (the only contact with the compiler is the build) and it keeps failing. That is what preserved the true accusation against navesz.github.io, whose `build` is `npm run data && tsc --noEmit && vite build`. `tipos` and `empacotar` stay Portuguese: they are the script names the rule has to accept in a Brazilian repository, and the whole point of this case.
